open.title: Treat TV episodes, not shows, as the unit in stats
open.excerpt: I think most Refract stats underrepresent TV viewing by treating 1 TV show as equivalent to 1 movie. A TV show makes sense as a single title, but not necessarily as a unit of consumption. Watching one movie and all 10 seasons / 236 episodes of Friends both count as one title, despite representing very different amounts of viewing. Suggestion: when a metric combines movies and TV, use watched movies + watched episodes rather than watched movies + finished TV show titles, where that makes sense. Importantly, this should be based on episodes actually watched, not the total episodes in a show. The Crew stats are a good example. Currently, someone who appears in 5 TV shows can rank above someone who appears in hundreds of episodes of a single show. Popular movie actors can also easily displace TV actors because each movie adds another title, while years in the same TV show still only add one. See my top ranking as an example, even though my TV watch time is 10x my movie watch time. Ideally, Crew could instead consider how many movies + episodes featuring that person I’ve actually watched. If I’ve watched 73 episodes featuring Actor A and only 3 featuring Actor B, that difference is represented even if both appear in one show. Runtime could theoretically be another way of weighting this, but it gets messy for Crew: being credited in a two-hour movie doesn’t mean an actor appeared on screen for two hours. Movies + episodes feels simpler and more understandable. As a side note, TMDB has more granular credits than show-level cast: regular cast at season level, with guest stars and other credits at episode level. So there is potentially data available to make these stats more representative. Crew is just the clearest example I’ve found, but the broader suggestion is to avoid treating 1 movie = 1 entire TV show when the goal is to represent how much you’ve actually watched.

open.title: Expanding game tracking to board games 🧩
open.excerpt: Hi, I believe there is a real opportunity to expand the current game tracking feature beyond traditional games by also including video games and board games. As a huge board game enthusiast myself, I see a strong community around this hobby and a real need to keep track of gaming experiences. The tracking feature could become much richer by allowing users not only to record the games they play, but also their individual gaming sessions. Some potential features could include: 📚 Creating a personal library of owned or played games; 🎲 Tracking played sessions (date, duration, players involved, number of participants); 🏆 Recording scores, rankings, and personal statistics; ⭐ Adding ratings, reviews, and comments after each game; 📊 Monitoring time spent on a specific game or type of game; 👥 Identifying gaming partners and keeping a history of shared sessions; 🎮 Applying the same approach to video games with playtime tracking, progression, completion status, and personal reviews. This could transform tracking into a real community-driven experience, allowing players to discover new games, compare experiences, and build a personal history of their gaming journey. Board games are currently experiencing strong growth and bring together a wide range of audiences. Adding this dimension could therefore attract a passionate and highly engaged community around the product. Cheers. Cever

open.excerpt: Hi, I believe there is a strong opportunity to create a new social discovery feature based on users’ preferences and interests: a “Taste Twin”. The idea would be to develop an algorithm that identifies, within the community, the users whose taste profile is the closest match to yours. This would go beyond your existing friends and allow you to discover new people with a similar universe of interests, based on a compatibility percentage. For example: 🎯 “Your Taste Twin is 92% compatible with your profile” 🔍 Discover people who enjoy the same games, genres, creators, or experiences; ⭐ See which preferences you have in common and where your tastes differ; 💡 Get inspired by their recommendations and discover new things that could expand your own interests. This feature could become a powerful social discovery engine. Instead of only connecting with people we already know, it would allow users to connect with members of the community who naturally share a similar mindset and passions. The value goes beyond matching profiles: a Taste Twin could become a source of inspiration, helping users discover new games, books, movies, or experiences through someone whose tastes are already proven to be close to their own. This could create deeper engagement within the community by turning individual preferences into meaningful social connections. Cheers. Cever

open.title: Removing the Activity tab
open.excerpt: I propose removing the Activity tab for a number of reasons. I have no problem with facilitating interactions between users and gamifying the app with badges and challenges, but I’m not in favor of this app placing a social network at its core. That’s exactly what happens when there’s a dedicated primary button that, perhaps unintentionally, leverages addictive design with a feed of activities and the ability to react to and comment on every single thing. We’re already inundated with apps that force us to stay on them as long as possible; I’d like this one not to be yet another one, especially since, judging by the developers’ good intentions, it doesn’t even need to be. Interactions between users are great, but I’d urge you to keep the culture of cinema, and the other future fields you’ve already mentioned, at the heart of the app. So my suggestion is to remove the Activity tab for good and organize the various activities within the app as follows: 1) Watched titles - these are already listed in the Collection tab and also in the Profile tab under Recent Activity, so it was already redundant 2) It doesn’t make sense to display your own ratings as a notification, so remove them 3) Unlocked Badges activities should be confined exclusively to the Profile tab 4) Participation and completed challenges should also go in the Profile tab 5) Notifications from other users should be merged into the notification bell at the top right of the home screen +1) Currently, the notification bell displays achievement notifications; those should also be moved exclusively to the Profile tab In summary: - All notifications regarding badges and challenges must be located in the Profile tab. - All notifications from other people should be in the notification bell. - Your own activities should appear only in your collection and/or profile. - It should not be possible to react to or comment on any of the above.

open.title: UI/UX Feedback & Suggestions for Refract
open.excerpt: Hi Refract team! First of all, thank you for building Refract. I've recently migrated from TV Time, and I'm really enjoying the app. The performance improvements over the last few weeks have also been impressive. After using the app for some time, I have a few UI/UX suggestions that I think could make the title pages cleaner and improve the overall experience. 1. Reorganize the title page layout Currently, the cast and crew section appears immediately below the title. While this information is useful, it feels overwhelming because it appears before more important information that most users are looking for. I think the information hierarchy could be improved. Suggested order Poster + Title Release year Status (Ended / Ongoing / Cancelled / Upcoming) External ratings (IMDb, TMDb, etc.) User actions (Mark watched, Rate, Favorite, Lists) Awards (optional) Cast & Crew Description This would make the page feel much cleaner and easier to scan. 2. Shorten the description The current description takes up a large amount of vertical space. Instead, I would suggest: Show only the first 2–3 lines. Add a "Read More" button for the full synopsis. This keeps the page compact while still making the information available. 3. Improve the rating experience The current 1–10 rating system feels a little overwhelming. Personally, I think one of these approaches would work better: Option A Switch to a simple 5-star rating system. Many users find this faster and easier than selecting a score from 1–10. Option B (my favorite) Replace numerical ratings with a recommendation-based system. Instead of asking users to score a title, ask how strongly they recommend it. For example: ⭐ Masterpiece 🔥 Highly Recommended 👍 Recommended 😐 Worth Watching 👎 Skip This focuses more on whether users recommend something instead of forcing everyone to assign a numerical score. It also reduces rating inflation and reflects viewing experience better.

open.title: Anime Architecture: Move away from Western TV structures to an AniList/MAL "Format" model
open.excerpt: Treating anime under the standard Western TV/Movie framework causes major tracking issues. 1. The Western TV Problem: Forcing an anime franchise into a single "Show" page with multiple seasons (Season 1, Season 2, etc.) doesn't match how anime actually releases. In anime, different seasons often have entirely different names, production studios, and metadata tracking rules. 2. The Movie Problem: Moving anime movies completely out of the Anime tab and into the generic Movies section completely breaks the chronological flow of a franchise. For series where a canon film bridges two seasons, forcing users to jump to an entirely different media tab ruins the tracking experience. Proposed Solution: Instead of forcing anime to fit the Western TV structure, treat Anime as a master umbrella category where every single release (whether it's a new season, a movie, or a special) is treated as a distinct entry, separated by an internal "Format" tag—exactly how dedicated trackers like AniList and MyAnimeList (MAL) handle it. Under the main Anime section, every entry would carry a specific format tag: TV (e.g., Jujutsu Kaisen Season 1 as its own entry) Movie (e.g., Jujutsu Kaisen 0 as its own entry) OVA / Special (Side stories and prequels) How this solves the franchise problem (The "Franchise Relations" View): Instead of nesting everything under one show page, each entry stands on its own but is linked dynamically. On any anime entry's page, a "Relations" section would map out the perfect chronological watch order across formats. Why this fits Refract: Respects Anime Culture: Dedicated anime fans heavily prefer the AniList/MAL structure because it allows them to favorite, rate, and track individual seasons and movies cleanly without things getting lost in a massive pool of live-action Western content. Cleaner Filtering & Sorting: Users can go to their Anime tab and easily filter their view by Format: Movie or Format: TV depending on what they are in the mood to browse.

open.title: Library UI/UX: Ability to rate individual seasons for TV Shows and Anime
open.excerpt: Since Refract already features seasonal tracking structures and averaging under the hood, it would be incredible to expand this into a front-facing UI feature so users can directly input, modify, and view their ratings on a season-by-season basis. The Problem: Right now, even though the backend architecture handles show structures beautifully, users often want to explicitly score a specific season (e.g., giving Season 1 a 9/10 but Season 2 a 6/10) rather than relying strictly on a single global show rating. Without a visible, dedicated field to view or tweak individual season scores, it hides a lot of the power of Refract's data handling. Proposed UI Solution: Inline Season Stars/Pills: Within a show or anime's main page, add an interactive rating component (like the standard star/point scale) directly inside the dropdown headers for individual seasons or next to the season tabs. Weighted Global Override: Since seasonal averaging exists, the app could dynamically display the calculated average as a placeholder for the overall show rating, while still allowing the user to manually override it if they choose. Profile Diary Integration: Let these explicit season ratings show up clearly in the personal history feed/diary when a user finishes the final episode of a season.

open.title: Having an undo button for personal activity which may have been unintentional
open.excerpt: The Problem: Accidental taps happen frequently when navigating through deep episode logs, the "Continue Watching" dashboard, or checking off movies. Currently, if a user accidentally marks an item as watched, finding and reversing that action requires drilling back into the specific media entry's sub-menus. If the user doesn't remember exactly which episode or movie they accidentally misclicked, it permanently skews their personal stats, history timestamps, and streaks. Proposed Solution: Introduce a small, contextual "Undo" button (or "X" icon) directly onto individual activity blocks within the user's personal Activity Feed / Diary tab. How it works in the UI: 1. Activity Feed Entry: Every entry in the user's private watch history row (e.g., "You watched: Episode 4 - Jujutsu Kaisen - 10 mins ago") gets a subtle, low-opacity button on the far right of the card. 2. One-Tap Reversal: Tapping this inline button instantly removes that specific log entry from the database, sliding the item out of the feed and correcting the user's total watch count and progress bars locally in real-time. 3. Safety Buffer: To keep it super clean and avoid double-accidental taps, the "Undo" icon can either change to a quick confirmation state ("Are you sure?") or simply feature a brief haptic tap to confirm the deletion.

open.title: Counter for how many people have "added" an item
open.excerpt: I use "consumed" with the meaning of "watched/played/read". Please help me find the correct verb in English 😭. The idea is to have a counter of how many people have consumed an item or have planned to consume it. It will enhance the social aspect of the app. - "Wow, I'm in the first 10 people to watch this series" - "1 million people have watched it, it must be good then!" - "why are 10k people planning to watch this new series? Let me Google it!" The 2 counters would be mutually exclusive, I think. Once the item is released, the planned counter will disappear and the "consumed" one will appear. To avoid making it heavy to compute (maybe), there could be steps in the counters instead of counting 1 by 1 each users. Something like: From 1 to 50: each new user (1,2,3...49,50) From 50 to 100: every 10 (50,60...90,100) From 100 to 500: every 50 (100,150...450,500) From 500 to 1000: every 100 (500,600...900,1000) From 1000 to 5000: every 500 (1000,1500...4500,5000) And so on. Heavy before 50/100, but after that it can be calculated not more than once a week. (Edit: probably it's easier to count the users as soon as they add an item, otherwise it would mean to check every item every time to know how many people added it) I think I got a formula that works after 50: From 5x10^z to 10^(z+1): every 10^z. (With z>=1) From 1x10^z to 5x10^z: every 5x10^(z-1). (With z>=2) Values between steps, like 3957, could be represented by the step before with a "+": "3500+"

Example: A show is currently airing weekly. I decide I want to wait until the season is complete. I move it to On Hold and select "Resume when the current season finishes airing". open.title: Import from CSV/Import Letterboxd Lists
open.excerpt: Request 1: Universal CSV Import I suggest adding the ability to import data via CSV files, including Refract’s own export format. While Refract already offers "one-tap" imports for major platforms, a manual CSV importer would allow for more flexibility, custom data migration, and reliable data recovery. Proposed Implementation: Import Menu: Add an "Import from CSV" option within the Data/Account settings. Field Mapping: A simple interface to map CSV columns (e.g., Title, Year, Rating, Date Watched) to ensure compatibility with different spreadsheet formats. Validation Step: A summary screen before the final import to show how many titles were matched, allowing for manual corrections. Why this is useful: This makes Refract truly platform-agnostic and gives users "data peace of mind." It ensures that users are never "locked in" and can easily restore backups or migrate from niche tracking spreadsheets that lack a direct API integration. Request 2: Letterboxd Custom List Import I suggest adding the ability to import personal Letterboxd lists from the "lists" folder in a Letterboxd data export zip. While Refract currently handles watch history and ratings, many users have curated extensive thematic lists that are currently lost during the transition. Letterboxd Data Export: The export zip contains a dedicated lists folder with a separate CSV for every list a user has created. Proposed Implementation: List Uploader: Within the Letterboxd import section, add a specific button for "Import Custom List (CSV)." Automated Creation: When a CSV is uploaded, Refract should automatically create a new list with the matching title and populate it with the identified films. Bulk Upload: Allow users to select multiple CSVs from their lists folder at once for a bulk migration.

open.title: Add “Plan to Watch” directly to the TV show status pane, with “Plan to Watch” meaning not started…
open.excerpt: Feature Suggestion: Add “Plan to Watch” directly to the TV show status pane I think “Plan to Watch” should be added directly to the TV show status pane/sheet. Right now, setting a show to Plan to Watch feels too restrictive. The current ways seem to be: - long-pressing a TV show card on Home - finding it through global search, then long-pressing the result - or using the bookmark icon from the main detail view That is not enough, because the status pane is where users would naturally expect to manage all major TV show states. I think the cleanest implementation is this: Plan to Watch = Haven’t Started = Not watched a single episode. So if a user selects Plan to Watch in the status pane, it should: - remove the show from Watching or any conflicting status - move it into the Watchlist - clear any watched progress by marking previously watched episodes as not watched This distinction matters because On Hold already exists, and that should logically mean the show has already been started, some episodes have been watched, and the user simply paused it for later. So the separation should be: - Plan to Watch = not started, zero episodes watched - On Hold = started, some episodes watched, paused for now If the status pane is meant to be the main place where users manage a TV show’s state, then Plan to Watch should exist there too as a proper first-class status.

open.title: Per-Platform Import History with Independent Undo
open.excerpt: The ability to undo imports should not disappear simply because another import from a different platform happened afterward. Right now, there are two import tools, Letterboxd and TVTime. I noticed that if I import from Letterboxd first, I am able to undo that import. But the moment I import from TVTime afterward, the undo option for the earlier Letterboxd import becomes unavailable. I do not think this should be the case. Undo history should persist across multiple import timelines regardless of order, just like Trakt handles import history more reliably. An import from one platform should not erase or override the undo availability of another. What should happen instead Keep an import history of at least the last 5 imports per platform, with each import treated as its own reversible action. Each import entry should show a summary such as: • how many shows and films were actually added • how many items were already in the library • how many could not be found • how many could not be matched properly • how many watched dates were restored • which titles were skipped or failed Ideally, each import history entry should also include: • platform source, such as Letterboxd or TVTime • date and time of import • whether the import was full, partial, or failed • a full list of films and TV shows that were not found or not matched • an Undo Import option tied specifically to that import action This would make importing far safer and far more transparent, especially for users moving data across multiple services. Right now, if one import removes the undo availability of another, it makes the entire migration process feel fragile. For users doing multi-platform migration, import actions should be independent, reviewable, and reversible.

open.title: Merge TV Shows and Anime in the Next Tab
open.excerpt: In the Next tab, I think TV Shows and Anime should be merged — or at least users should have the option to merge them permanently. I understand that the platform treats TV Shows and Anime as distinct categories overall, and that makes sense in broader browsing and classification. But in the Next tab specifically, both serve almost the exact same functional purpose: tracking episode-by-episode progress, showing watch history, the next episode to watch, and upcoming releases. Because of that, separating them here makes the navigation feel a bit cluttered and unnecessarily divided. A better approach would be either: 1. Merge TV Shows and Anime into one section in the Next tab, since both are serialized content, or 2. Let users choose whether they want them merged or separated, with that preference saved permanently until they decide to change it. The important part is that the preference should stick. Users should not have to keep toggling it every time they open the app. This would make the tab feel cleaner, faster to navigate, and more practical for people who view both as part of the same ongoing episodic watching flow.

I don’t want this show to be in my “watching” list as my type a personality would go bonkers with it not being clean, however I would like record that I watched that show. I could use Dropped or On Hold…… but I feel dropped is for shows that I tried and didn’t like. On hold is for something I will get back to which I wont be unless there is another crossover and it still an ongoing show. I am open to suggestions on how to use the current indicators. Sometimes I get stuck on how I think it means and need a nudge.

shipped.title: Now, Release Date, Manually, Unknown
shipped.excerpt: This has been mentioned and suggested before, but mostly as having the possibility to set watch date to Now, Release Date or Set Date Manually. This has also been implemented and shipped. 👍 I'd want add Unknown Date to that. So everywhere you can set the Watchdate there should be four possible options: - Now (this should be the default, unless you chose to set another option as your default) - Release Date - Set Date Manually (maby having the possibility to set just the year, year and month, and full date (had the idea to maybe even have the opportunity to set it to what querter of the year or "early" "mid" "late". Also Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter (though season might might be unclear. Is Winter October-December or January-March? This also depends on your location. Anchorage has obviously not the same period of seasons as Rome, New Delhi or Melbourne) - Unknown Date This'd be great for all those shows, films, and whatever will be added, you know you've watched but not when.

shipped.title: On Hold
shipped.excerpt: First I am assuming “On hold” is like the Tv time “watch later” tag. If so, could we please have this shown some where on the continue watching…. Of course this is mute if this is on the Next Tab I cant see yet. If “on hold” is not comparable to “watch later”m then can we add “watch Later”? I am using this tag for a show that has aired in the UK but not yet in the US, because I can’t watch it yet.

shipped.title: Option to stop watching
shipped.excerpt: (starter message inaccessible)

shipped.title: Possibility to mark multiple season as watched ?
shipped.excerpt: I just spent 10min to mark all OnePiece season as watched. Maybe add the possibility to mark multiple season as watched ?

shipped.title: Quick option to set watch date to 'Release Date' for better history accuracy
shipped.excerpt: Currently, when marking a movie as watched, the only options are "Today" or manually picking a date from the calendar. The problem is, for older movies, manually scrolling back years in the calendar to set the correct watch date is time-consuming. Because of this, many users end up using "Today," which clutters the recent history with movies actually seen years ago.

shipped.title: Refract Lists should support descriptions
shipped.excerpt: Lists on Refract should have the ability to include a description, similar to how Letterboxd handles lists. List descriptions are useful because they let users add: • context • purpose • rules/criteria • notes about ranking or ordering • personal commentary Without that, lists can feel more like just a title plus items, when sometimes the meaning behind the list matters just as much as the entries themselves. I think adding descriptions would make lists feel more expressive, informative, and complete.

shipped.title: Remember library sorting & filters
shipped.excerpt: I’d love the library page to remember my sorting/filter preferences. right now every time i open the app it resets to “last updates”, but i usually sort by release date and would like it to stay that way. It would be great if it could remember the last sorting (and filters) i used, so whenever i change them it just keeps that setup until i change it again. hope this makes sense 😅

shipped.title: Review Tags
shipped.excerpt: The option to have more tag options for reviews. Would be a nice addition.

shipped.title: See how many users added your list
shipped.excerpt: That we can see how many users added a list that we created. Doesn‘t need to show who it was… but would be cool. Or also leave a comment or reaction to someones list ☺️

shipped.title: Skip review - even not on continue
shipped.excerpt: Can we add skip review toggle for even when not on continue watching. I am not a reviewing kinda person.

shipped.title: The monthly wrap shouldn't be a one time view
shipped.excerpt: I saw today that there’s a monthly wrap feature in the app. But it disappears the first time you view it. It should remain accessible for at least a short while at the start of the month (e.g. only the 1st day or 1st week of the month). If the user would like to remove it, they can do so by clicking the "x". I couldn't find a way in the app to view it again without having to clear the app data.

shipped.title: Track special episodes
shipped.excerpt: Special episodes are not imported and can’t be tracked. Special episodes can also have a sequence/be part of a season (see screenshots) but I don’t know if TMDB supports special episode positions (& critical to story flag) like TVDB does.

shipped.title: Turkish? When?
shipped.excerpt: (starter message inaccessible)

shipped.title: Upcoming section with only the very next episode of each show
shipped.excerpt: > I know this section is still a work in progress and I've commented another post with this suggestion, but I wanted to make a separete one to avoid beeing lost. Instead of listing by default all the release dates of each episodes of each show (basically now everything is there), I'd list only the very next episode of each show => it would compact the list and give a clear picture of what is coming in the next weeks/months. The final result could be something very similar to the bottom section called "later" in the tab "Upcoming" (first image) This suggestion view could be displayd by setting/toggle, like "full/complete/expanded" for the current view and "short/syntesis/contracted" for the one suggested BUT IMHO, the suggested one should be the only one here, since the complete info of all airing dates can be found in the "calendar" (for all series/movies combined) and in the series/movies page (for a focus on a specific series). As it is now I find it redundant: 3 places with the same info Having multiple episodes of the same series listed here (as currently implemented) takes screen space and doesn't give the full picture of what's really "Upcoming". You can see that tomorrow and in 8 days (info already known since it want's a "finale" the previous episode) and so on you'll have an episode of a series, but unless you scroll down (possibily a lot down if you are watching multiple series togheter) you won't know that in 17 days there's the first episode of a new season of another series (TV Time screenshot as an example that has the same problem). Example: You're watching (only) 7 series, each one airing once a week => 7 lines per week. If a 8th series has a premiere in 1 month (let's say 4 weeks) you'll have to scroll down 74=28 lines before finding this info instead of just 7 (with the suggestion) => 1 series, 1 item in the upcoming list (or grid as TV Time, if we want to do that, but I'll leave it to another suggestion) Sorry for the long post 😇

shipped.title: Upcoming TV episodes tab and notifications
shipped.excerpt: Sorry I this was already raised, I really enjoyed the upcoming tv shows tab on TV Time. Is there any plans to do something similar and also get alerts/notifications when a tv episode/show you follow releases a new episode?

shipped.title: Use source “date added” when importing watchlists
shipped.excerpt: After importing both TV Time and IMDb, my watchlist order is all over the place. I’m used to sorting by “Date Added”, but after import this gets set to the import date, so everything appears incorrectly ordered. Both TV Time and IMDb exports include the original date a show or movie was added to the watchlist. Can that field be used during import to preserve the correct ordering?

shipped.title: View shows
shipped.excerpt: (starter message inaccessible)

shipped.title: Watch time expressed in y-m-d-h
shipped.excerpt: I don't know you guys, but if I read 573 days and 6h of time spent watching I can't really visualise how much it is. More then year, of course, but not much more. Moreover, those 6h compared to the count of days (with the current format) are really insignificant and could be removed (I don't say I'm "21yo and 4 months"...) Instead if it was 1y 6m 28d 6h (years, months, days, hours) it's much immediate to understand. the counters for the durations not reached shouldn't be displayed untill needed => 251d should be 8m 11d (without "0y" in front) This will make that rectangle a bit larger than the other 2 for ratings and items tracked, but they seem much larger than they need to be. we could make them with "dynamic" spacing, getting larger/smaller as needed.

shipped.title: Watch without a specific date
shipped.excerpt: Just an idea, but it could be cool to click on watch and be able to set only as watched (without a date) or something like that, this is for previous Movies o TV Shows that we haven't tracked and we don't remember the exact date of watch. Similar to when you only click watch on letterboxd, it doesn't set a date.

shipped.title: Weekdays on dates
shipped.excerpt: Add weekdays on dates. Instead of "Apr 23" it should be "Thu Apr 23", for instance.

shipped.title: You can leave the app during the import
shipped.excerpt: It’s unclear if imports happen server or client side. A message prompting the user that they can leave the app and will be notified once the import is finished will be appreciated

shipped.title: Track Collection / Sagas
shipped.excerpt: Hi, it would be interesting to have the list of all the movie collection (sagas) that we have begun. It will allows us to know if we are missing a movie to watch in this collection with a progressive bar for example. To expand this feature, it could also apply in the books area. It will tell people when a new book from the collection has been released. Waiting your thoughts on it 🙂
